text:
alex.w: Heads-up — a customer using the payments sample app hit duplicate charge events. Root cause looks like the SDK replaying a POST after a 429 that happened during token refresh.

jia.chen: ugh. can you paste the minimal log?

alex.w: sure — timeline: client sends /v1/payments -> gets 429 (rate). SDK tried to refresh token, refresh succeeded, SDK retried the original POST without idempotency key. logs: `POST /v1/payments 429 -> token_refresh ok -> RETRY POST 200 order created`

samir: that matches a class of unsafe-replay bugs. when auth refresh is in the middle of a request, the replay might re-execute non-idempotent ops. did the sample app set an idempotency key?

alex.w: no, sample app uses naive wrapper for new users so it didn't set one.

morgan: SDKs should probably treat "retry after auth refresh" as a different class from transient network retries. safe defaults: do not auto-replay mutating requests after a token refresh unless an idempotency key is present or the route is marked safe.

jia.chen: agreed. current Node and Python SDKs differ: node added a guard last year, python hasn't. that's a parity gap. we should standardize behavior and document it.

samir: proposal: change default policy to: 1) if status==429 or 5xx and request failed before request body was streamed, allow retry with backoff+jitter; 2) if auth refresh occurred, require either idempotency key or explicit opt-in flag `allow_auth_replay: true` to replay mutating requests. also add telemetry event `replay_blocked_by_auth_guard`.

alex.w: SG. can we also set a small jitter bound for retries by default? current jitter ranges vary between SDKs. suggest uniform random in [100, 700] ms for first retry, exponential backoff thereafter.

morgan: +1 on telemetry. default jitter 100-500ms seems safer for low-latency flows. make it configurable per-client.

jia.chen: I'll open a parity PR for python to match node behaviour and include a feature-flag `sdk.replay.auth_guard` (default true). PR will: update retry docs, add unit/integration tests using the sample payments app harness, and add a note in the onboarding README.

samir: test checklist: 
- replay after 429 during token refresh for POST with no idempotency key (should be blocked)
- same scenario with idempotency key (should replay)
- streaming upload vs small JSON POST behavior (no replay if body streamed)
- telemetry event emitted with reason code
- e2e sample app updated and smoke test runs on CI

alex.w: for the sample app update, i'll add a warning in the quickstart: "Always include an Idempotency-Key for mutating operations. SDKs will block unsafe replays by default." Also add a short snippet showing how to set idempotency key.

jenkins-bot: build queued for branch: devex/replay-auth-guard (job #482)

jia.chen: assigning self to the PR. aim to land in next sprint. tagging @morgan @samir for review.

morgan: will review. also let's add a small migration note in changelog (breaking in edge case: previously some SDKs retried silently)

alex.w: thanks all. i'll patch the sample app and notify the customer with the mitigation steps (add idempotency key until we ship the fix). :thumbsup:

ci-bot: integration tests triggered for branch devex/replay-auth-guard — current status: running

samir: after landing, follow-up: consider adding a runtime flag to allow opt-in replay for high-throughput partners with idempotency guard proxies. not default.

jia.chen: noted. I'll include an RFC section for partner opt-ins.

alex.w: closing loop — will post a short PR link here once ready.
